notes.title: Dev Update
notes.content:
Hi everyone - I just wanted to check in, since some of you (quite rightfully) called me out for not doing so on a regular basis. The main update is that I've started to gameplan something that I've wanted since the beginning of development - co-op. It was a feature I thought I would wait on until after coming out of EA, but it was such a central feature in my mind, and I'm way past worrying about deadlines. Releasing it without co-op would feel incomplete, so I'm giving that a go. My goal is to make the next update include it, so you faithful followers can kick it around and see how it works. Zero timetable for it, but I'm very excited about giving it a go. I hope you all are too!

Goose

notes.title: Dev Update 11/16/2018
notes.content:
Slow but steady, I've been working on expanding the fire modes for the player. My goal is to have 10 separate fire modes/types, which are changeable on the fly, for example, fire, ice, poison, void...some as direct damage, others as AOE, others as debuff.  The idea is certain enemies have vulnerabilities, which isn't earth shattering. The additional idea is that certain damage types work synergisitcally with some debuffs. For example, void damage might cause a poisoned enemy to spread poison to other enemies around it.

Onward...

Michael

notes.title: Dev Update; June 7, 2017 / Beta Access Code
notes.content:
I'm back at it after an amazing month in Barcelona. Even though I stayed mostly away from the comp, I did have time to sit with pen and paper and map out some technical aspects of the missions. I also had some fun getting deeper into the lore of the game. So I've got two notebooks full of HOI goodness to start implementing.

I've also tidied up the developer console I've been using to test the new mission and hero framework, and it is now ready for everyone with the Developer's Edition. In it, you can play with the 3 main hero classes (each with 3-4 skills), along with 3 basic units types.

If you're interested, the Beta Access Code is: devtestinghoi. 

[b] Please bear in mind, that build will only work if you have the Developer's Edition[/b], even though anyone can opt in. I'd hate for you to waste the dl bandwith.

My push now is to get the missions linked together, with hero and unit XP, and other stats, carrying over between missions.  Once that's set, I'll turn my sights back to the city building and its defense. My continued thanks for everyone's patience, encouragement and feedback!

Michael

notes.title: Dev Update, May 2017
notes.content:
It’s been a long few months getting the main hero archetypes set, but they are finally about right. There’s still quite a bit of fine tuning and polish necessary on them, but functionally I’m happy with them. On top of this, the new squad feature is working great - there’s a handful of basic units that all move and attack with the hero they are assigned to - and enemies are working better than I expected they would at this point. So, with a nice stable of good and bad NPC’s, I’m finally ready to start putting together a series of maps in which to turn them loose.

But first, I’m taking a break until June. I need it to recharge the batteries, so I’m in Barcelona until next month. If anyone happens to be here, ping me and we’ll grab a cafe con leche. When I get back I’ll lay out the plan moving forward.

notes.title: Dev Update; April 3, 2017
notes.content:
Massive progress since the last update - the three main hero archetypes are done along with a handful of their special abilities. Heroes also now have the ability to attach basic units to them to form squads. This means now the player can issue orders to heroes (rather than managing tons of units) and their squads will follow the hero and execute those orders.

I haven't pushed this to the main branch, but I do have a testing branch up. Once that's ready for public consumption I'll add the instructions for accessing that branch to the Developer's Edition main menu.

The basic roadmap from here is - create a more detailed level with multiple areas to attack and defend (the current testing level is linear and doesn't create much drama), add in some heavier enemies, add in some more of the 2nd and 3rd tier hero skills, and once that's all in place and relatively bug free, let that loose to everyone.

Michael

notes.title: Dev Update: March 10, 2017
notes.content:
I just pushed a fix for Brimley (PC version), it should be good to go again. Mac update should be coming shortly.

Although I've been quiet on the boards, I've been hard at work on the design side of the game.  The new assault style has yielded great feedback (many thanks to those of you who offered great ideas for moving forward). With the suggestions and my own revelations, the game is getting more and more solidified and streamlined in getting to the heart of the strategy and action.  I am very excited about what the next major update will show; from the discussions I've had with the most vocal supporters of HOI, it will tick all of the boxes that you've all been looking for.

I'll probably post non-fix updates in large pieces, but I'll play it by ear and see what makes sense.

Michael

notes.title: Dev Update; Jan 26., 2017
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/6876777/10156e20bb3966ec3a82e73089f4ed179a44ec35.png[/img]
[i]The Void Treader, Stalking a Minion (Discussed Below)[/i]


Things are progressing well - I just pushed an updated build for the Developer's Edition; all changes are in the New Assault menu item. Here's a recap of what's been added and included there:

Basic swordsmen and archers can be teleported in, and they gain levels (visualized by gold bars on their armor).

Merastalks, the ent-like healer unit is available, and it has a basic group heal ability (along with a big staff with which to whack bad guys).

On the bad guys' side, the wolves are still the staple of this level. Headshots are working.

Minions have been added as a bad guy unit. I'll be constructing variations off of this model, as it's pretty cool and the folks who made it did a fantastic job of making it modular and customizable.  So, in essence, if human-ish is the race of the good guys, these minions are the race of the bad guys. This doesn't mean there won't be other types, but I'll be getting a bit more mileage out of the minions than other models.

The most exciting addition (for me, at least) is the Void Treader. This is a hero class that utilizes the power of the void that exists between the world of Issachar and our own. The base class is a bit rogue, a bit mage, and as the character levels up, you can choose how to specialize. The first ability is Void Strike, where the Void Treader teleports behind a bad guy and double shivs it, killing it instantly:

[url=http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/6876777/10156e20bb3966ec3a82e73089f4ed179a44ec35.png][img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/6876777/aa92fddb55c9326498d7d0ddb6f5183a808a0163.png[/img][/url]



[url=http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/6876777/67496abf663c49a9f35a11d060957759f836512d.png][img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/6876777/b5c4d4ddbd4c4e12b24e11e69df2e6459dcf0386.png[/img][/url]



[url=http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/6876777/4b4d858877fd70317bcb9e3871d3f69468f16308.png][img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/6876777/97f1e59e8e09be4683433add82ce018a3122afb4.png[/img][/url]



[url=http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/6876777/36b22e4fcedeb7dd0094e7674ccf1680ce4f4bca.png][img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/6876777/bd775bc240d586373a4346e87e892d199bb615bd.png[/img][/url]


So all of that's in the Dev Edition, New Assault menu option. I'm close to swinging that over to the base edition; I'll do that once I'm sure my AI doesn't have any major issues. For now, if you encounter game breakers, please let me know; animation issues are almost all known (like the eyes and mouth of some units), so assume I'm working on those.

Thank you for your continued support and patience! It's been a long haul so far, but it's taken the many revisions to get the game where it should be, in essence to "reveal itself." I couldn't have gotten to this point without all of your advice and criticism (all of it well taken), so, as always, thank you and keep it coming!

Michael

notes.content:

I made the splash video skippable (although it was loading the main menu in the background, so I'm not sure you'll move any faster), and added graphics options to the main menu. You can now adjust your settings with more specificity.

I've gone back and forth on what to do next but I'm on a roll getting the units added back after the last pivot, so I'm going to keep going with that.

Michael

notes.title: World Map Update
notes.content:
I just pushed builds to Steam, and Humble should be uploaded by tonight. The main change is the world map and the Kingdom HUD.  Check it out, and the overall game cycle should start to make some sense.  I decided to pare down resources into Gold, Food and Materials, with Materials representing all building materials.  Dividing materials into more specific resources just felt like busy work, and I'm not interested in getting into the minutiae of crafting. I want building to focus on the strategy of what to build, not on tracking down different resources.

I decided to alter the plan and work on building in provinces once they are liberated.  That means once you've liberated the Argent Coast, and get together some Materials, Gold and Food, you'll be able to place buildings there that augment that province's production and other benefits.

Check it out and let me know your thoughts!

Michael

notes.title: Developer Update; August 1, 2016 - HOI available this week until August 5
notes.content:
So, big update for those who have access. If you don't, now's your chance! I'm putting the widget back up for this week to bring some more people on board. Here's the link:

[url=http://www.bluemanaentertainment.com/?p=64] Heroes of Issachar [/url]

Read the instructions closely - you can get immediate access offsite, and a Steam key, but the Steam key won't unlock until the official launch.

Before I get into it, one instruction that is in this build but a little hidden - Press "U" in the Argent Coast to teleport back to the Citadel.

OK, so what's in this update -
First, I added the very beginning of the game. It's a rough sketch of it, but it paints a bit of the narrative, introduces you to some major NPC's, and mostly gives you information about just what is going on in this fantasy world.

Second, I added a new province to explore. The premise is pretty basic, which I'll leave for you to discover, but it's a fun little romp around a province with a few bad guys and a dungeon.

Third, there's a new addon for the crossbow, the frost cannon. It's not totally new, I've had it in a few versions, but this one is juiced up. It'll fire multiple shots of ice that will track enemies themselves. So basically you can fire it without really aiming and the shots will do the work.

Fourth, I added two new enemies. One is a big nasty dude I haven't named yet. You'll know it when you see him, he's got a spiked ball and chain. The other enemy are flying skulls. They'll kamikaze you, so better shoot them out of the sky.

Fifth, Save and Load Games. Test the heck out of this for me, because I'm sure there will be bugs that crop up. 

There are still plenty of things that need work. Most of all, animations. NPC's won't look at you, won't talk during convos, etc. I'll get to that, but since that's purely aesthetic, it's on the back burner. The other big issue is pathfinding. Sometimes the bad guys will just get flustered and not move, sometimes they'll run to places they shouldn't be. I've got a fix in the works, but it didn't make it into this build. So for now, enjoy shooting extremely stupid bad guys :)

Also, load times for scene changes are a little long for my liking. I'm working on that, but for now, if a screen looks frozen, it might not be, especially when teleporting, or opening the world map.

Up next - more bad guys, more good guys, and more add ons for the crossbow. I really want to get the tug of war more interesting, along with dungeons and other places to explore. So for the next 30 days my focus will be on bad guys, and the corresponding add ons that counter their strengths. In the meantime, please let me know what you think - either from a gameplay standpoint or if anything is crashing for you.

Thanks!

-Michael

notes.title: Developer Update; June 23, 2016 - EA Release Date, Roadmap
notes.content:
First, what did I do with my 30 day break? I made a game! With the help of my best friend we knocked out a casual racing game that can be played solo or split screen. It tested well with adults all the way down to five years old. If you feel like some low stress racing of rubber duckies, or just want to support my HOI efforts, check it out (releases on July 14, 2016):  [url=store.steampowered.com/app/491110]Duckie Dash on Steam[/url]

http://store.steampowered.com/app/491110


Now I'm back from my sabbatical, refreshed for HOI, and I've already made tons of progress on the next province. Where the first one (Tranask Island) is very structured, the next one (Argent Coast) is a bit more open. The basic goal is to locate a unique hero knight and recruit him for the cause, but there will be a number of different points of interest to explore. My ultimate goal is that once the player has secured the province, they will have a small settlement to grow as they see fit. It will, in a sense, be a bit sandbox-y, although the settlement (and hopefully one day city) will be able to supply resources and troops for the larger war effort. It's ambitious but doable, and I'm excited to see what you all think about it.

So, getting the Argent Coast through its first iteration is my current goal. That means there are some caves to explore, some people to interact with, some bad guys to kill and the main purpose of recruiting the knight is working. It also means some of the aesthetics are set, but it doesn't mean every last rock and tree looks great, or that there aren't ways to break it. The goal for that to be finished is July 31.

The other major feature I need to get set is what happens between the intro video and the first action of the game. Some players' feedback was that it wasn't totally clear what to do. So I'll be working on that once the Argent Coast is finished.

If you missed the limited sale last month, keep a look out around July 31, because I'll probably do another one then.

And, I have locked in an Early Access release date: November 3, 2016.

Thanks for continuing to follow my progress, I'm really optimistic about where we are headed!

Michael

notes.title: Developer Update; May 22, 2016
notes.content:
So the soft launch is underway, and so far the response has been amazing. If you're interested in grabbing Heroes of Issachar right now, you can do so here: [url=http://www.bluemanaentertainment.com/heroes-of-issachar-developers-edition/] Heroes of Issachar Developer's Edition [/url]

So the two main questions, and then a roadmap below. First, what does buying it through that link get you?
[list]
[*]Immediate Access to the most up to date build (PC and Mac)
[*]Steam key
[*]Special in-game items reserved for purchasers of this edition
[*]Direct access to me for gameplay discussions, feedback and game design roundtables
[/list]
Please note, the Steam key will unlock the game in Steam, but it cannot be downloaded until the official Steam launch (these are the Steam rules, not mine, and I intend to abide by them closely since, besides you the gamer, Steam is the last people I want to get mad). You will be able to download the game immediately through the widget in that link.

Second, why not just launch Early Access?  Because we only get one launch, and I want to add a few more features before launching. I also want to update all of the media (screens and vids) to show off everything that's new. And, I'm hoping to get some media coverage to increase visibility prior to the Steam launch.

Roadmap

So I've been working non-stop on HOI since January, and with the current build in play, I need a bit of break so I don't burn out. I've got a ton of ideas I want to implement, but stepping away for a bit will allow me to approach them fresh. So for the next 30 days or so, I'll be here in the forums to discuss the game, and if there's anything game-breaking I'll be sure to work on fixing it.

So what does someone obsessed with making video games do for a break? They make video games, of course :) I've got a tiny little couch co-op game I've been kicking around, so I'm going to jam it out, cleanse the HOI palate, and come back fresh at the end of June.

So, during that time, the most help you can give me is to let me know what features you would like to see implemented first when I pick things back up. I'll start a thread in the discussions to get your feedback, but the best place to send ideas is to the email given when you purchase the Developer's Edition through the link.

I say this often, but please know that I mean it - thank you for your continued support. It has been a long road so far, but the game is really starting to take shape, and even though moving towards launch feels like nearing the end of a long cycle, it also feels like the beginning of a new one where we mold this game into something special.

Michael

notes.title: Developer Update; May 10, 2016
notes.content:
Quick update, with a more detailed one to follow - Last night I pushed a major update, and if everything works as expected, I'm planning on doing a soft launch through my website within the week. That launch will inform whether the game is ready for a Steam launch, and if it is, we can then talk about when that should happen.

So, if you've got access, please really dig in to this build! In it you can:

-Recruit Heroes
-Send them on Quests
-Level them up
-Equip them with items (in this case only a weapon)
-Attack one province, bringing along one Hero with you

Building in the province has been simplified to focus more on the action. I have another Sandbox Mode in mind that will allow more detailed building at a slower pace, but that's for another discussion.

Instead of building single units at a time, you now build platoons of 20. I suggest you create a platoon before attempting to storm the enemy camp...

At any point in the province attack, press H for help - there's still some things going on that might not be apparent.

Good luck!

-Michael

notes.title: Developer Update; April 7, 2016
notes.content:
I thought I'd take a breather from the furious coding I've been doing to give an update and a bit of a roadmap. Things are going really well - for the last month or so I've been working on nothing but the hero quests and the loot attached to them. I'm happy to say everything is working really well. Although the UI isn't in final form, it's close enough where I can let everyone with access start tearing into it.

Next on my list is getting the UI set for the player's personal level up's and skill upgrades. After that I'll get the world map set so the player can select different provinces to build/attack. Once that's set, HOI will be very close to what I'd call the full experience. 

There are just a few bugs I'm aware of that I couldn't live with myself if I didn't fix before flipping the Early Access switch. Then there's the business of updating all of the media on the storefront because it's all pretty outdated, along with starting to get a little buzz going before the launch, since I only get one crack at that.

That's the thumbnail sketch of what's going on - as I've said before, thank you for following my progress and your words of encouragement. Even though there are still some major hurdles to jump, that light at the end of the tunnel is getting brighter and brighter!

Michael

There are just a few bugs I'm aware of that I couldn't live with myself if I didn't fix before flipping the Early Access switch. Then there's the business of updating all of the media on the storefront because it's all pretty outdated, along with starting to get a little buzz going before the launch, since I only get one crack at that.

That's the thumbnail sketch of what's going on - as I've said before, thank you for following my progress and your words of encouragement. Even though there are still some major hurdles to jump, that light at the end of the tunnel is getting brighter and brighter!

Michael

Or they might die, so make sure they're suited for the task...

I'm going to pin a discussion thread for anyone who has access; Any questions, issues, ideas, etc. should go there instead of the private group we were using, that way everyone can chime in whether they have access yet or not.

Michael

notes.title: Developer Update; July 19, 2015
notes.content:
Testing is going really well, below is the roadmap I gave to that group.  I'm still adding to the testing group, so if you've offered to help already, I'll still be sending invites over the next few weeks. From the testing group post:


Where we're headed:

RIght now I'm working on the building placement system. Currently the buildings snap to a grid, but I'm working on allowing the player to move and place and buildings wherever there is space, with fluid movement. Along with that I'm working towards implementing city walls. I've also got on the drawing board a bad guy called the Festering Bomber, a nasty winged creature who floats towards structures and explodes.

Upcoming features:
-City Walls. I want this to be A+. Placement, movement, moats, etc. My solution right now is not good. I'm working on it.
-Scouts can find dungeons, which the player can then crawl for loot.
-New Unit: Knight
-Villages: Explore to find them, then win their trust (Quests) to get caravans bringing resources to the city.
-New Hero: Goblin (a reformed bad guy, he's got gadgets and weapons)
-New Crossbow Addon: Fury Spray - Infected enemy attacks bad guys
-New Crossbow Addon: Fireball Launcher - Magic noob tube
-Magic Gauntlet: Besides the crossbow addons, the player will be able to augment his abilities by modifying a magic gauntlet they are given. Things like bullettime, run speed, jumping, levitating...they'll all be modifiable with the guantlet.
-Melee. This is something that has come up a few times and it's absolutely gonna be a big part of the game. But it's also really hard to do well. So I want to tackle that when I have extended time to dedicate to it, rather than try to chip at it here and there.

These are the short list items, there's a ton more in the hopper, especially with repect to exploration. The other major item on the list is the end game for each province, which has the player assembling his army, including siege weapons, and assaulting the main enemy stronghold.

notes.title: Developer Update Jan. 31, 2015
notes.content:
Hey everyone, update time: January's been slowing going. I had two separate game-breakers I spent time fixing, but they did get resolved. For February, I'm working more on the enemies. Specifically, I'm working on getting one of the opposing heroes fully functional, top to bottom, AI through special abilities. This is a good time to go into how the enemies will work (at this point; all of this is subject to change if it sucks).  First some background: 

Each region has a few different things in it. 1) A starting place where you'll rebuild the city, 2) enemy outposts that have portals (spawn points) 3) the enemy stronghold (their main base), and 4) dungeons, buildings and other places to find resources, loot, and captured townspeople.

There are two types of friendly NPC's, Common and Heroes. Common NPC's are your resource gatherers and generic military NPC's. Heroes are unique NPC's that you rescue throughout the game and reside in your main castle. At any given time, you can have 4 Heroes accompany you whereever you go.

Conversely, there are two types of enemies, Common and Dark Champions. Common enemies are found in dungeons, and they spawn at outposts. They vary between ranged and melee, and some have preferred targets, like buildings or gatherers. Dark Champions are unique enemies who each guard an outpost. Dark Champions have a range of abilities, and will do more than just attack until they die. They will retreat to the outpost if their health is low, and stage strategic attacks against the city accompanied by Common enemies. Killing a Dark Champion will allow the player to destroy its portal, weakening the enemy presence in the area, and provide the player an area to build an outlying town. The first area will have anywhere from 3-5 Dark Champions defending it.

The other thing I'm working on is traps. I've got two types I'm looking at - castle defense traps and individual traps. Castle defense traps are ones like explosive barrels hidden where enemies might attack from. Individual traps are ones like a tripwire that you can set by hand, or by firing it from your crossbow into a distant wall.

So, since you've made it this far, tell me, what kind of traps would you like to see in HOI?

Michael

notes.content:
Hi all, I just wanted to drop in with a quick update. It was a good week of dev on HOI, although I lost a day and half fixing the building placement logic. I thought it was all set, but it wasn't.  The good news is that it appears to be working perfectly now. Buildings, walls, towers, cannons, roads, street lights - they're all working as expected.

The day/night cycle is working too.  I posted a raw, high res video here: 

http://youtu.be/r_rCSBGTV08

Steam only allows up to 1080p, so if you want to see what HOI looks like in 4k, there it is.

So, here are some things in the game I'm happy with and some things I'm not:
Good - The buildings that I've got completed are all working well. Blacksmiths build weapons and armor, barracks spawn units, the Rogue's Guild will run missions to raid enemy treasuries, the Scouts will discover hidden treasure and entrances to dungeons and reveal them on the player's map.
Bad - The economy is not robust enough yet. I'm not holding out until it's perfectly balanced - that's what I'm hoping you all will assist with - but right now there's not enough buildings to make this first scenario interesting yet.

Good - The bad guys are all working as expected, up to this point. They attack who they should attack, their pathfinding is adequate, they take local damage (headshots at this point), the animations all fire when they should and generally look pretty smooth.
Bad - They're boring. Sure, there's some variety between ranged and melee, and some have specials like poison or slowing, but they're not smart and they don't provide a different enough challenge between them. Not to worry, I've got plenty of ideas on how to make them better, but it's going to take time. The big question is how much "better" the bad guys need to be before launching EA. I'm still debating this, but your insights are appreciated.

Good - The player's special abilities all work great. Stuns, DPS, AOE, Heals - all working as they should.
Bad - Again, not enough variety. This goes along with the bad guys issue since good abilities give the player choices in how to defeat certain enemies.

There's plenty more to discuss, like how the friendly NPC's will work, both the generic units and heroes, but I'll dive into those in a separate update. Thanks!

-Michael
